The notion of 'docility' emerges as a corollary, implying that behavior must be coherent across parts to be effective. Immanent determinants are the final causal variables in this chain, inferred from observation rather than directly measured. These primitives form a hierarchical causal structure where higher-order states (determining tendency) constrain lower-order responses (immanent determinants). The failure mode occurs when systemic integrity breaks down, causing fragmentation of behavior. In GSI, these concepts map to latent variable inference and probabilistic causality. In GSE, they define state transitions within a constrained system. The mathematical duality lies in treating behavior both as a molar phenomenon and as a set of interacting subsystems.
